To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cholinergic factors in rat footpad extracts are biochemically different from CNTF, CDF, and the cholinergic factor from skeletal muscle.

(1) extracts from rat footpads induce the differentiation of sympathetic neurons from a noradrenergically to a cholinergically innervated phenotype; (2) a 22-26 kDa soluble protein is the major component of this extract; and (3) this protein is immunoprecipitated by antibodies to ciliary neurotropic factor (CNTF) but is distinct from CNTF.
a cholinergic differentiation activity is present in extracts of rat sweat glands and is distinct from CNTF, CNTF mRNA or CNTF protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying the regulation of neuronal differentiation.
the identification and characterization of the molecules that induce the cholinergic phenotype in sympathetic neurons during development in the rat footpad.
identifying the molecules that induce the cholinergic phenotype in sympathetic neurons and determining their role in normal development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CNTF is a component of the cholinergenic factor in sweat glands, but that it is not the sole factor.

CNTF and a second factor, yet to be identified, are the major cholinergenic differentiation factors present in footpad extract and that the CNTF present is not produced by sweat glands but is associated with sensory fibers.
CNTF and a second cholinergic differentiation molecule are both present in the footpad extract and both contribute to the cholinogenic activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cholinergic factors present in extracts of developing footpads are distinct from CNTF, CDF/LIF and the differentiation activity in skeletal muscle.
multiple cholinergic differentiation activities are present in footpads.

the cholinergic induction activity is present in the footpad extract but is not CNTF and that there is a second cholinergic inducing factor present in the extract that is biochemically different than CNTF.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multiple cholinergic differentiation activities can be obtained from different sources and that the major factor in the footpad is not CNTF, but rather a novel cholinergic differentiation molecule.
the cholinergic factors present in the footpad extract are distinct from the factors previously described.
the sweat gland extracts are a complex mixture of cholinergic differentiation activities and that the major factor present is related to, and distinct from, Ciliary neurotrophic Factor (CNTF).
